tutorial.title: Destructuring
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to destructure Objects and Arrays.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Using items from arrays is common in games, but it gets messy if you always rely on index numbers.

Use the first and second elements of enemies to fill in the if and else if conditions.

Make sure to pick enemies[0], followed by enemies[1].

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Destructuring lets us assign array items to variables so we can use them like any other variable. It is a clean way to simplify game code.

We store new variables in [] and assign them to the original array enemies.

Make sure to pick enemies, followed by enemies.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
The first element inside the [], playerName, corresponds to the first element in the array, Astra.

After destructuring, we can use playerName like any other variable.

Make sure to pick playerName, followed by playerName.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
The second element inside the [], health, corresponds to the second element in the array, 100.

Make sure to pick health, followed by health.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Finally, the third element inside the [], spawnPoint, corresponds to the third element in the array, Forest Camp.

Make sure to pick spawnPoint, followed by spawnPoint.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we do not want to destructure every element in the array, we can save the rest in anyOtherVariable by using ... before anyOtherVariable.

Make sure to pick . followed by . and then ., anyOtherVariable.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
The , inside the [] skips variables in the destructuring array's first and second positions.

We extract the array's third element in spawnPoint.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by ,.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the basic process of destructuring an array?

Using square brackets [] to store the variables corresponding to the array elementsUsing curly braces with the exact name of the element

Using square brackets [] to store the variables corresponding to the array elements.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What kind of datatype is extraLoot?

An arrayAn object

An array.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of the commas in this code?

Skip the first, third, and fourth elements of the arrayKeep the remaining items we are not using in the destructure in a new array

Skip the first, third, and fourth elements of the array.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's destructure this array using the variables playerName, health, and spawnPoint.

Make sure to pick playerName,, followed by health,, and finally spawnPoint.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's destructure the first element of this array with the variable levelId and keep the remaining elements in the array moreInfo.

Make sure to pick levelId, followed by . and then ., ., moreInfo.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Destructure the array's first, second, and fourth elements in the variables levelId, playerName, and favoriteItem.

Make sure to pick levelId, followed by playerName, and then ,, favoriteItem.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Destructuring simplifies the use of values, and we can use this functionality with game objects too!

We can extract a game object’s values into new variables using braces {}.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
The three variables inside the {} correspond to the three values in the object.

Use the exact names of the properties for the variables in the destructuring.

Make sure to pick name, followed by health, and finally score.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We use the original property name, a colon, and a new name if we want to use variable names that differ from the object’s properties.

Make sure to pick item1, followed by :, and finally enemyType.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
To separate the first and second values, and keep the rest of the object together, add ... and otherStats after the first two properties.

Make sure to pick ..., followed by otherStats.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the basic process of destructuring an object?

Using curly braces with the exact name of the object propertiesDeclaring a variable and assigning the object directly

Using curly braces with the exact name of the object properties.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can we customize the variable names we use in an object destructure?

Including a colon and the new name next to the variable name to changeNot including

Including a colon and the new name next to the variable name to change.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What datatype is rest?

An objectA string

An object.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Destructure the level object.

Make sure to pick name, followed by difficulty, and finally enemiesQty.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
We received an object with a variable name that's too general. Store the sprite property as playerSprite.

Make sure to type playerSprite.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
We split out playerSprite but need to keep the rest of the object. Store these additional properties in extraInfo.

Make sure to pick . followed by . and then ., extraInfo.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
The destructuring syntax makes it possible to unpack values from arrays, or properties from objects, into variables.

Let’s explore some applications of destructuring: setting default values, and sending destructed parameters to functions.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can set default values when we're unsure whether an unpacked element value exists, or is set to undefined.

Make sure to pick =, followed by 3.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like with arrays, we can set a default value to ensure an object has a value for a property we need.

Make sure to pick playerName, followed by =, and finally "Guest".

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can destructure arrays when we are defining the function parameters.

Notice the first two items of the enemyTypes array as destructed parameters for spawnWave.

Make sure to pick first, followed by second.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
The announcePlayer function needs playerName and playerClass from playerProfile. We destructure the object to define the function parameters.

Make sure to pick playerName, followed by playerClass.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can set a default value to ensure health has a value inside the function.

Make sure to pick health, followed by =, and finally 100.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
If you set a default value for a variable in a destructuring, but the unpacked element already has a value, what will be in the variable?

The unpacked element valueThe default value

The unpacked element value.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of using default values?

Setting a value in case the element doesn't exist or is set to undefinedChanging the values of all the unpacked elements

Setting a value in case the element doesn't exist or is set to undefined.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What syntax do you use to pass destructed parameters from an array to a function?

square brackets []curly braces {}

square brackets [].

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the function announcePlayer print?

Player joined: Remi the Rogue, health is 34Player joined: Rogue, health is 34

Player joined: Remi the Rogue, health is 34.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Our level objectives array needs four objectives. Add the default value "find a potion" for bonusObjective.

Make sure to pick =, followed by "find a potion".

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the default value for spriteSheet. Assign www.gameassets.com/sprites/player.png.

Make sure to pick =, followed by "www.gameassets.com/sprites/player.png".

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send the third and fourth items of lootDrops as destructed parameters for showLootMessage.

Use the variables names rareItem and legendaryItem.

Make sure to pick rareItem, followed by legendaryItem.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send enemiesDefeated as a destructed parameter for getBonusScore.

Make sure to type enemiesDefeated.
